The row-image predecessor has the same cap/chord normalization and strict incidence. It places every actual f in the stated open cube slab, so the roots and cyclic products are positive and f_i<2.

Independently checked the square identity by taking a matrix with column i equal to sqrt(u_i)e_i minus sqrt(1-u_{i+1})e_{i+1}. Its Gram matrix in row coordinates has diagonal one and cyclic off-diagonals -f_i/2. The column matrix determinant is sqrt(prod u_i)-sqrt(prod(1-u_i)), with a minus sign from the three negative entries in the cyclic term. Expanding the Gram determinant gives 1-(sum f_i^2+f_1f_2f_3)/4, independently verifying all constants and signs.

For g=f_j+f_k the cubic sum is f_i^2+g^2-(2-f_i)f_jf_k, which is at least f_i^2+(2+f_i)g^2/4 by f_jf_k<=g^2/4. Dividing the resulting bound on (2+f_i)g^2/4 by 2+f_i>0 yields g^2/4<=2-f_i. Equality is equivalent to both zero cubic deficit and f_j=f_k, since 2-f_i is strictly positive.

At u=(1/2,1/2,1/2) the row vector is (1,1,1), giving both cubic and all three row equalities. The same-batch signed-row predecessor of the row-image theorem already gives the individual row inequalities by a different deficit; the new claim is the joint cubic identity and its direct equality link.
